notes.title: Early December update
notes.notes:
Hello, everyone! 

2021 is quickly coming to an end, and there aren't enough hours in a day to cover everything we've 
already begun working on and everything we're eager to start with. Although we keep discovering 
new challenges every day, the enthusiasm and the work drive are running strong. We're very proud 
of the development progress so far, and we are excited to let you in on a few newest changes to 
Pastel:

[olist]
[*] Looking back at the initial idea of creating a visually pleasing adventure puzzle experience, 
we've noticed a slight disbalance between the puzzle and the adventure aspect. So what did 
we do to add more 'venture' into the adventure? A whole [b]new mechanic[/b], of course! From 
now on, Pastel will be able to use [b]Possession - an ability to possess a nearby creature and
use its natural abilities to overcome obstacles[/b]. Ethically, of course. No creatures were 
harmed during the creation of this mechanic. 
[*]  How about the ability to interact with the obstacles in a much more elaborate manner? We 
got it covered! [b]Some of the obstacles can now be destroyed and repaired to complete 
given tasks.[/b] Ruined bridge ruining your fun? Nothing a few wooden boards won't fix. 
Collect, repair, and progress!
[*]  Additionally, [b]we have tweaked the labyrinth[/b] area with a few redesigns that we plan on 
implementing within the game.
[*]  We all love [b]collectibles[/b] for the sake of collecting, but in the world of Pastel, everything has 
a role. For that reason, we have assigned a more active one to each collectible symbol in the 
game. To keep it charmingly challenging, e[b]ach symbol now holds equal importance in 
solving narrative puzzles[/b]. Their completion will no longer be possible without all of the 
necessary pieces.
[*] [b]The Ghost World[/b] has woken up! This previously passive area [b]became richer for some 
interactive elements[/b]. You will now have the opportunity to explore it more while searching 
around for interactable parts of the environment and discovering their secrets.
[*]  In the end, what's all of this worth if it isn't looking its best? For that, we are working on 
improving the adventure with a [b]large-scale texture overhaul[/b] and showing some love to the 
third - no less important - part of Pastel: its visual experience.
[/olist]
A lot of the upcoming changes, and we are equally ecstatic to show you the progress we made on 
adding new levels... As soon as we get the new levels to cooperate with the game's environment. In 
the current stage, freshly added parts are clashing and require cleanup before the proper 
walkthrough. While we work hard on overcoming these obstacles, a friendly reminder that we 
appreciate your support! 

Keep up with the updates, and feel free to reach out for any questions you may have.

Thank you!

notes.title: Pastel: Blind Karma re-design
notes.notes:
Ever since we first had an idea for Pastel: Blind Karma,
we have imagined a colorful, vibrant, dynamic adventure. And while we are well on our way to bringing that vision to you, it's always a good thing to leave some room for backtracking and addressing some things that could have been done better.

And we did exactly that! So what exactly did we do? Check it out below:

1. Pastel is now more enthusiastic about her mission! We have added a bit of a skip to her step by improving the jumping mechanics and the interaction with objects (It will now rely on indirect connection rather than simple, rigid animations).
2. We have even shown the shaders some love. They are now upgraded from presented assets to being handmade!
3. Color is love. Color is life. You will enjoy an improved color blend on grassy surfaces and ground textures. 
4. Overhauled! Trees and grass are all goosed up, making the entire image richer with a lot more tone. Real eye-candy.
5. Updates rock! No, really. We have updated our rocks. They are now much well behaved.
6. High five, but down low? Got a lower-graded software? It doesn't mean you should be getting a lower-graded Pastel: Blind Karma experience! We have optimized our textures to support your setup as well.
7. Prefabs can be fabulous! Especially the reconstructed ones. Tune in for an increased optimization and frame rate!
8. Cutting it close on the levels. Levels will now be more densely packed with a lot more puzzles to do! We need activities! What's all that empty space in between good for anyway?
9. Literary enthusiasts, rejoice! More puzzles mean more diversity, and more diversity means adding text puzzles. In these types of puzzles, players will need to collect different words/symbols to beat the stage. Each encountered symbol will be registered in your dictionary to be used to decode the messages! Venturing through the levels, you will eventually run into obstacles that can be destroyed only by choosing the correct sentence out of the suggested ones while using the symbols registered to decipher them. Sure, you can play it by chance and guess the answer but be warned! Making a mistake will lead to a reshuffling of the task into a new one.    

So much work to be done! Our development team is working hard to organize all of the prefabs and the content. And while there are some issues with the optimization, we are highly optimistic that we will keep it up on schedule! The biggest problem we are encountering is that the models are not cooperating and not functioning as we would want them to.

This means that assembling the first level correctly and offering you the best possible experience with all listed improvements will take more time and patience. Bits and pieces need to be put into place. Nothing is irrelevant.

We are also using this opportunity to thank you for the endless patience and support you constantly show for this project. Hopefully, we will be able to come back to you with more details regarding the entire process (and, of course, the finished product) soon!

notes.title: Introducing Yuni Jang, one of the Pastel Artists!
notes.notes:
[h2]Hello everyone![/h2]

While work on our game continues, we want to begin introducing you to the team behind the game.
To start things off, we're going jump straight into our art team!

[h3]The Art Team[/h3]
The art team consists of Yuni Jang (South Korea) and Ilya Sipyagin (Russia) and together they bring a unique blend of both cultures and inspirations to the game. In this first team focus, we're going to look at Yuni and her experiences working on Pastel!

[h3]What is your process for drawing?[/h3]
Our basic character creation always starts out with a hand-painted version! 
Normally at the beginning of the creative process, I would search for inspiration from a few sources, and after that use my imagination to get a consistent idea of what I want. Once I've got that, I draw the initial sketch. 

Once I'm happy with the sketch, I'll then pass it over to our 2D artists who convert it into digital art, or sometimes I give the sketch directly to the 3D artists.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38253336/3a171dad948479b48347236a998b6457914544d2.png[/img]

When I worked on drawing Pastel (our heroine), we followed all of the steps from this process. I draw a couple of different sketches and passed that to our 2D artists who adapted it to a digital sketch, then finally our 3D modeler created the final character.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38253336/d2bec9b00e4d7df3866f4d60000428eab92d5b12.jpg[/img]

[h3]Do you work together on designs, or do you work separately?[/h3]
Ilya and I tend to work together (as there are many designs, objects, and characters in the game) so when we start to work on an object or character, we would discuss everything from the background story to the appearance, then one of us would start to draw it, but we'd always exchange feedback with each other.  

[h3]Do you or Illya specialize in a specific art style?[/h3]
I would say that I prefer geometrical or traditional approaches to my art while Ilya is highly interested in biological fantasy! 

[h3]Approximately how long does it take you to draw a scene for Pastel?[/h3]
That really depends on what the art is and how complex it is. The quickest that I've completed something was a few hours and the longest can take over a week. However, on average I'd say about 2-3 days is the normal duration.

[h3]What was your favorite part of the game to draw?[/h3]
My favorite part was creating the Samsara stage in the game as it shows the many worlds in our game through the symbols and its actual form! 

I'll share an image of it, so do note that every image is connected to one of the game levels!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38253336/ead0ce1f10c65e832e778c3d3c050dd3a3e0f8ff.png[/img]

And this is what it looks like in-game
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38253336/78c7f01fce275da654de7005e7edd0d868b5ae46.jpg[/img]

[h3]What is your favorite model to draw?[/h3]
It has to be the main character design! From the first step to the very last, creating Pastel (the character) was extremely demanding, but it was very fun! While drawing her, we had to put a lot of thought into creating her as we had to think about her emotions during each part of the story, how that would impact her looks, what her backstory was, and so on!

I'd say that throughout the entire process, we (both of us) really have become fully attached to her!

[h3]Was there anything that you disliked drawing?[/h3]
Honestly, we don't have any dislikes. There were a few images that were really hard to draw, and so gave us a few concerns, but even with that, we didn't dislike anything.

Personally, I found drawing the level 6 arena boss to be very hard, mainly because we lost our amazing first sketch. That said, looking back at everything now, I actually think that the final re-drawn version came out better than the original!

Here we have the art side of things
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38253336/a31a9c39b49d130d9249a06ff1577ef8834fd7e4.png[/img]

And here is the in-game version
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38253336/50d099c55b31c30e86fd318cc65cdf3db5c08bce.jpg[/img]

[h3]What do you use to draw for Pastel?[/h3]
Both of us prefer classical pencil drawing!
Digital painting is really lovely, but to me, it lacks emotions. Obviously this is an entirely personal opinion, but I believe that art should start out on paper first, and only after that should we make the digital version. The reason is simply that I feel that if you start on a digital version right away, you can't really get the full set of feelings and emotions as you would by drawing it on paper first. [i]Again, this is just my personal thoughts, there will definitely be others that disagree and that's totally fine![/i].

[h2]And to end this, do you have any tips for people who may want to become a game artist?[/h2]
The simple thing that I want to recommend to everyone is to directly draw what you imagine in the first place. 

Just start your drawing, then add more and more to it, step by step, sketch by sketch, and as a result, it will transform to a proper, world created by your imagination.

notes.title: Welcome to Pastel: Blind Karma!
notes.notes:
[h1]What is Pastel: Blind Karma?[/h1]
Pastel is an Adventure-Puzzle game, but to dive a bit deeper, it is a single-player game that draws influence from Asian cultures and was inspired by popular games such as Rime, Journey, and Firewatch.

Our name comes from an amalgamation of the words Past and Teleport and serves as both the name of the game and also the name of the main character, who happens to be a Gumiho, a  legendary fox creature from Korea.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38253336/f427036c1ddd76e85373537c7b7925f6104cf744.png[/img]

What's more, time-travel and teleporting through timelines are both key aspects of our game, so Pastel is a very fitting name for us!


[h2]The Gameplay[/h2]

Now we're getting to the good stuff, talking about what our game will be like. As you may have guessed from our introduction, time travel plays a very big role in the game. The game starts with Pastel waking up in the middle of ruins, taken over by nature and time. As she wakes up, she realizes that something is wrong, she has very little recollection of how she got here and of what happened.

All she remembers is that a calamity took place a long time ago, she had some connection to it, and in the midst of the chaos, she was thrown into the darkness. After that, nothing.

As you play the game, you will gradually recover bits of Pastel's memory and powers, and ultimately deduce that she is still on the same planet, but has been thrown into the far future.

Her goal: Explore the land where she finds herself, unlock more memories and powers, and slowly jump back in time while building herself up until she can ultimately return to her time and fix whatever has happened.

[h2]Game Footage[/h2]

Though we are still in development, we are now working towards a playable demo so we've got some videos of the game that we can share with you.

[h2]The Music Of Pastel[/h2]

This is something special that we put together when we first started to talk about our game. We wanted to share the game OST with everyone, so we've created a special [url=https://soundcloud.com/pastelthegame]SoundCloud page[/url] that we keep updated.

We'd also love to know what you think about it, so please feel free to give us your feedback.
